lead.name: Food Inflation Risk
lead.trend: Materialising — CFPI 5.52% in July, seen >5% headline by Sept
lead.summary: The primary transmission channel, and it is now printing. Consumer food inflation reached 5.52% in July (from 4.78% in May and 5.32% in June), lifting headline CPI to a 19-month-high 4.45% — driven by vegetables and spices (ginger +84%, garlic +35%, onion +23%) with the West Asia war feeding through to transport and restaurants. A below-normal August–September (IMD <94% LPA) keeps pulses, oilseeds and vegetables under pressure even with adequate aggregate supply. Peak food-price pressure lands in Oct–Dec, coinciding with the strongest El Niño phase; economists see headline CPI above 5% by September and flag a possible RBI hike as early as December.
drivers: CFPI already at 5.52% (Jul) and rising — vegetables and spices leading, not a broad-based shock
Below-normal August (IMD <94% LPA) hits the month carrying ~29% of seasonal rain and ~20% of kharif sowing
Peak El Niño phase (Oct–Dec) aligns with the peak food-price window and pre-Budget sensitivity
West Asia war passing through to transport (4.43%) and restaurants (7.72%) — a second, non-monsoon leg
A positive IOD in September is the offset that could ease the monsoon channel (the 1997 template)

channels.name: Drought Risk
channels.note: ~44% reservoir storage, recovered from 26% in early July but below normal; south/east basins critically low.

channels.name: Agriculture Risk
channels.note: Kharif sowing gap narrowed to ~3% YoY (from ~23% in June); pulses, oilseeds and the south/east still exposed.

channels.name: Heatwave Risk
channels.note: El Niño years skew hot; pre- and post-monsoon windows the concern.

channels.name: Flood Risk
channels.note: El Niño suppresses the heaviest monsoon flooding vs La Niña years.

channels.name: Water / Hydro Risk
channels.note: Storage below the seasonal normal; southern and eastern basins the concern for hydro (NHPC, JSW) into rabi.

risk.riskInference: The dominant channel for India in 2026 is no longer a forecast — it is a print. Food inflation has climbed for three straight months to 5.52%, and the analytically important feature is the timing alignment: the peak El Niño phase (Oct–Dec), peak food-price pressure, unfavourable base effects, and pre-Budget sensitivity all converge in the same window, with economists already pencilling headline CPI above 5% by September and a possible December RBI hike. The reservoir recovery removes the supply-collapse tail but not the price pressure. The single mitigant worth tracking is the September IOD: a positive turn would ease the monsoon leg, though the West Asia crude channel would remain. This is the channel to position around, not the headline monsoon number.
